method: shapely Douglas-Peucker with preserve_topology=True, applied per cut piece after the cookie-cut and before int16 quantisation

areaClasses.reason: audit-measured baseline: area error -0.005 % (lm) to -0.013 % (m), well inside the 0.05 % gate
a piece above 1e6 km2 carries most of the nodes and none of the narrow features; half-way to the audit's 0.05 degree measurement, which alone reaches -0.030 % on lm
continent-scale pieces only; the audit measures -0.030 % (lm) at this tolerance applied to every piece, so applying it to the few largest is far inside the gate

sm.reason: shallow marine is an environment class whose mapped boundary is a modelled facies limit, not a coastline, so the audit's 0.05 degree variant is the defensible tolerance for it: the audit measured -0.030 % area error with 0.05 degrees applied to every piece, well inside the 0.05 % gate, and the per-piece 0.1 % guard, the narrow-feature witnesses and the protected North Sea window still apply unchanged

classAreaClassesReason: the areaClasses ladder above is the default for every class; a class named here replaces the whole ladder. Only the ladder is per class - the vertex cap, the per-piece area guard, the protected windows and the narrow-feature witnesses stay shared.

vertexCapEscalation.reason: a piece still above the cap after its class tolerance is retried at double tolerance until it fits or the maximum is reached; the escalation is recorded per piece in the quality-control record

lostPiecePolicy.reason: node reduction runs per connected component. A component that Douglas-Peucker empties, that is still outside perPieceAreaErrorPercent at minimumToleranceDegrees, or that loses a hole or splits, is emitted with its unsimplified ring instead of being distorted or lost. Measured before this rule a 202 km2 island vanished from an 842,373 km2 piece 1.8 degrees away while the piece's own area stayed inside 0.1 %; the gate then measures pieces genuinely dropped, and the quality-control record counts every component that took this path.

quantisation.note: the quantisation step is an order of magnitude below the 0.02 degree baseline tolerance, so simplification, not quantisation, sets the geometric error

protectedWindows.reason: the Viking Graben, Central Graben, Moray Firth and Zechstein margin are 20-60 km wide; a 0.02 degree (2.2 km) tolerance is a large fraction of their width and the basin edit contract is written against these outlines

the iceland basin contract draws land from the Natturufraedistofnun Islands 1:600,000 bedrock outcrop, already simplified at 0.02 degrees by scripts/research/palaeo_coastlines_iceland_ops.py against declared 60 and 100 km uncertainties. A second node reduction inside this window would move a coastline the contract derives and pins, and the island's fjord-scale detail is already at the class floor

narrowFeatureWitnesses.description: east-west transect across the Viking Graben at 60.5 N
east-west transect across the Central Graben at 56.5 N
east-west transect across the Inner and Outer Moray Firth at 57.9 N
transect across the southern Zechstein basin margin from the southern North Sea into the north German basin

perPieceAreaErrorReason: no single piece may move its own spherical area by more than this; a piece that does is retried at half the tolerance down to minimumToleranceDegrees. Without the guard the worst mountain interval measured -0.0696 % against a 0.05 % gate while the class average was -0.0112 %: a few narrow belts carried the whole error.
